```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
```

## Context

This analysis evaluates the performance of three sorting implementations:

- **Sequential quicksort** — standard recursive quicksort
- **Parallel quicksort** — multi-threaded version using Pthreads (thread level = 10)
- **Built-in libc qsort** — C standard library reference

Each implementation was run **30 times per array size** to allow reliable statistical estimation (Central Limit Theorem). Array sizes range from 100 to 2,000,000 elements. The order of experiments was **randomized** to avoid cache bias.

---

## Loading data

```{r load-data}
# Set this path to the results/ folder relative to this file
# If you open the .Rmd from the analysis/ folder, this path is correct
seq_df <- read.csv("../results/sequential.csv")
par_df <- read.csv("../results/parallel.csv")
lib_df <- read.csv("../results/libc.csv")

seq_df$method <- "Sequential"
par_df$method <- "Parallel"
lib_df$method <- "Built-in (libc)"

df <- rbind(seq_df, par_df, lib_df)
df$method <- factor(df$method, levels = c("Sequential", "Parallel", "Built-in (libc)"))

head(df)
```

---

## Summary statistics

```{r summary}
# 95% confidence interval using t-distribution
summary_df <- df %>%
  group_by(size, method) %>%
  summarise(
    n        = n(),
    mean     = mean(time_sec),
    sd       = sd(time_sec),
    se       = sd / sqrt(n),
    ci_lower = mean - qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * se,
    ci_upper = mean + qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * se,
    .groups  = "drop"
  )

summary_df
```

---

## Performance curves with 95% confidence intervals

```{r plot-main, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
ggplot(summary_df, aes(x = size, y = mean, color = method, fill = method)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper), alpha = 0.15, color = NA) +
  scale_x_log10(
    breaks = c(100, 500, 1000, 5000, 10000, 50000, 100000, 500000, 1000000, 2000000),
    labels = scales::comma
  ) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::scientific) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Sequential"      = "#E63946",
    "Parallel"        = "#457B9D",
    "Built-in (libc)" = "#2D6A4F"
  )) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Sequential"      = "#E63946",
    "Parallel"        = "#457B9D",
    "Built-in (libc)" = "#2D6A4F"
  )) +
  labs(
    title    = "Quicksort performance: sequential vs parallel vs built-in",
    subtitle = "Mean execution time with 95% confidence interval — log/log scale",
    x        = "Array size (log scale)",
    y        = "Execution time in seconds (log scale)",
    color    = "Method",
    fill     = "Method",
    caption  = paste("Machine:", Sys.info()["nodename"], "— Date:", Sys.Date())
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 10)
  )

ggsave("../figures/performance_curves.png", width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 150)
```

---

## Speedup of parallel over sequential

```{r plot-speedup, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
speedup_df <- summary_df %>%
  select(size, method, mean) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = mean) %>%
  mutate(
    speedup_parallel = Sequential / Parallel,
    speedup_libc     = Sequential / `Built-in (libc)`
  )

speedup_long <- speedup_df %>%
  select(size, speedup_parallel, speedup_libc) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols      = c(speedup_parallel, speedup_libc),
    names_to  = "comparison",
    values_to = "speedup"
  ) %>%
  mutate(comparison = recode(comparison,
    "speedup_parallel" = "Sequential / Parallel",
    "speedup_libc"     = "Sequential / Built-in (libc)"
  ))

ggplot(speedup_long, aes(x = size, y = speedup, color = comparison)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  scale_x_log10(
    breaks = c(100, 500, 1000, 5000, 10000, 50000, 100000, 500000, 1000000, 2000000),
    labels = scales::comma
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Sequential / Parallel"        = "#457B9D",
    "Sequential / Built-in (libc)" = "#2D6A4F"
  )) +
  labs(
    title    = "Speedup relative to sequential quicksort",
    subtitle = "Values > 1 mean the alternative is faster than sequential",
    x        = "Array size (log scale)",
    y        = "Speedup (sequential time / method time)",
    color    = NULL,
    caption  = paste("Machine:", Sys.info()["nodename"], "— Date:", Sys.Date())
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 10)
  )

ggsave("../figures/speedup.png", width = 10, height = 5, dpi = 150)
```

---

## Variability across repetitions

```{r plot-boxplot, fig.width=11, fig.height=6}
ggplot(df, aes(x = factor(size), y = time_sec, fill = method)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.8, linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Sequential"      = "#E63946",
    "Parallel"        = "#457B9D",
    "Built-in (libc)" = "#2D6A4F"
  )) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::scientific) +
  labs(
    title   = "Distribution of execution times across 30 repetitions",
    x       = "Array size",
    y       = "Execution time in seconds (log scale)",
    fill    = "Method",
    caption = paste("Machine:", Sys.info()["nodename"], "— Date:", Sys.Date())
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

ggsave("../figures/boxplot_variability.png", width = 11, height = 6, dpi = 150)
```

---

## Conclusion

```{r conclusion}
crossover <- speedup_df %>%
  filter(speedup_parallel >= 1) %>%
  slice_min(size, n = 1)

cat("Parallel quicksort becomes faster than sequential starting at size:",
    ifelse(nrow(crossover) > 0, crossover$size, "not reached in this range"), "\n")
```

The parallel implementation introduces thread creation overhead that dominates for small arrays. The crossover point — where parallelism starts paying off — depends on the number of available cores on the machine. Running this same script on different machines allows direct comparison of these crossover points.
